title: What should we automate? Lessons from socio-technical systems
content: History repeats itself, prompting us to reflect on our learnings. As we consider task automation, particularly with the speed rise of #AI, it is essential to identify the optimal tasks for automation while evaluating the impact on individuals involved. The emergence of new #AIautomation solutions necessitates a thorough assessment of the #socialsystem.

An insightful video explores the analysis conducted by Eric Trist and Ken Bamford in 1949 at the Tavistock Institute. Their study of miners' work led to the development of socio-technical systems. However, we must critically examine whether teamwork, as described by Trist in his seven principles, is truly feasible. The question of how far we can progress in "self-management" remains pertinent.
Determining what to automate and what to retain poses a significant challenge in creating a smooth and efficient organization.
Geert Van Hootegem Francis Devisch Ezra Dessers
excerpt: Automation starts with understanding the work and the people doing it. Ives reflects on teamwork, self-management and socio-technical systems.

title: The Customer’s Truffle: connecting customer needs with the organisation
content: Announcing...thankfully...it's that time again :) My next book is ready to be read.

How can we deliver what customers ask for? That's what "The Customer Truffle" is about. It provides insights into how you can adapt the inside to deliver what's needed on the outside. A mix of Industry X.0 technologies and old, increasingly less familiar approaches helps us understand how the organization does what it does.

"Read this book as an (ultimate) synthesis that reveals its richness through integration. This integration provides fertile ground for “value & sustainable” organisation. Exactly what our economy, society, industry, their leaders and operators are craving."
Geert Van Hootegem Luc Semeese Luigi Neirynck
